prospects.stage_1_notes: Not public domain, and HARD CONSTRAINT 3's death-year/pre-1928 test does not apply cleanly here: the About page (fetched 2026-09-21) states 'This translation is by the Evangelical Lutheran Church of England (2016). prospects.notes: Found via Discord alongside the Wittenberg source (see luther-small-catechism, imported 2026-09-21) — Tapani (ELCE) offered this contemporary translation in the same conversation. Queued per Keith's request 2026-09-21 specifically to hold the open questions somewhere durable, not because Stage 1 is expected to clear soon. Open questions for Keith, in rough order of how blocking they are: (1) LICENSING MODEL GAP, the real blocker — CC BY-SA 4.0 requires visible attribution and requires share-alike licensing on derivative works; Stromata currently treats every text as functionally public domain (no license field on texts/collections, no attribution display distinct from source_attribution/editorial content, no CC badge anywhere in the reader UI). Importing this without solving that isn't a copyright risk so much as a promise-breaking one — the license terms wouldn't be honoured even though the text says they will be. (2) SHARE-ALIKE ON GENERATED CONTENT — does a note_draft written by reading this CC BY-SA text count as a derivative work that itself needs a CC BY-SA notice? Genuinely unclear; needs a real answer (Keith's own judgement or actual legal advice), not an agent's guess. (3) DEDUP COLLISION RISK, mechanical but real — pipeline-import.mjs skips a text whose normalised title already exists under an author whose name normalises the same (shared logic with dedup-draft-texts.mjs, via scripts/lib/dedup-match.mjs). small-catechism-luther just imported 'Small Catechism' under 'Martin Luther' — a chapter here titled identically would likely be silently skipped at Stage 5a as a duplicate, not imported and not erroring. If this is ever unblocked, each chapter's title needs to read as a different work (keep the '(ELCE contemporary translation)' qualifier through to the actual text titles, not just this queue entry), or the skip needs to be a deliberate reviewed choice rather than a silent one. (4) FETCH MECHANICS, the easy part, already solved — the site exposes a clean WordPress REST API (GET /wp-json/wp/v2/pages/<id>) that returns content.rendered as near-chrome-free article HTML, just a 'Previous section:'/'Next section:' link pair per page, far simpler than Wittenberg's masthead/nav/contact blocks. Page ids already identified by fetching the page list (2026-09-21): 22 Preface, 23 Ten Commandments, 24 Creed, 25 Lord's Prayer, 26 Baptism, 27 Confession, 28 Sacrament of the Altar, 29 Daily Prayers, 30 Table of Household Responsibilities, 212 Christian Questions with Their Answers. The last two are sections the Wittenberg edition doesn't carry, worth keeping in mind if this ever gets built — they might be worth pursuing on their own even if the main catechism text is held back. (5) RELIABILITY, minor but should be budgeted for — direct HTTP requests to the site intermittently (roughly 1 in 3 during a short test burst on 2026-09-21) return a Cloudflare bot-challenge page instead of content, both on the REST endpoint and on plain page loads. A real fetch implementation would need retry-with-backoff around this, not just a single request. source_type 'wordpress_rest' is a placeholder label describing the fetch approach found above — it is not wired into fetch-texts.mjs's SOURCE_SELECTORS and must not be until (1) and (2) are actually resolved. Running Stage 2 against this entry as it stands would produce output nobody has reviewed against a license nobody has decided to honour.

prospects.stage_1_notes: Requested by a reader on Discord (2026-09-22), who noted the library had Keble's National Apostasy but not The Christian Year. COPYRIGHT: Keble d. 1866 (<1900). Original English verse, first published 1827 — no translator, so no translation-copyright question at all. Gutenberg ebook #4272, ed. Henry Morley, released 2003. SOURCE VERIFIED, not merely reachable: fetched pg4272.txt and read the header — 'Title: The Christian Year / Author: John Keble'. This is the check the Spurgeon All-of-Grace mis-fetch exists to enforce; a 200 alone would not have been enough. GENRE CALL — deliberate, flip it if you disagree: set to Poem rather than Hymn.
